s.area.s.s: For owners who rent out their apartment in a WEG

s.diag.h: From bank statement to rent account
s.diag.p: One line of the CAMT.053 file is checked, matched to a tenancy and posted to the rent account. You can split or reverse an entry.
s.g1.p: Finalized statements and records can no longer be changed.
s.g2.p: You fix mistakes with a reversal and a correction, without deleting records.
s.g4.p: Access to a person’s data and erasure requests with retention checks. Protected records remain; final erasure after expiry is not currently automatic.
s.g5.p: Organizations are separated by row-level database rules and permissions. Privileged operational access requires additional organizational controls.
s.g6.p: Neither this site nor the app uses analytics trackers.
s.m1: Properties and units with year built, areas, meters and meter readings
s.m2: Leases with base rent, operating-cost advance payments and deposit
s.m3: Graduated rent, index-linked rent and rent changes from a set date
s.m4: Rent charges prorated by day, a rent account for each tenancy, open items
s.m5: Tenant changes and deposits: agreed, paid, repaid
s.m6: Betriebskostenabrechnung (operating-cost statement) per lease, as a PDF
s.q1.a: Nothing. That goes for the hosted service once it launches and for installing it on your own server. The source code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. You can download it there for your own installation.
s.q2.a: Yes. In addition to CSV, DATEV and PDF outputs, an organization archive contains authorized records and original files. It does not include all internal evidence; access and re-import have limitations. A complete service-exit handover needs separate verification as described in the DPA draft.
s.q3.a: Current source limits the free hosted service to 20 properties, 200 units and 2 GiB of document storage per organization. These hosted quotas do not apply to self-hosting; usable scale also depends on hardware and data volume.
s.q3.q: How many units can Verwalino handle?
s.q4.a: Yes. Docker Compose starts Verwalino together with PostgreSQL, on a laptop just as on a server.
s.q4.q: Does it run on my laptop?
s.q5.a: No. Document analysis and property questions are optional. Current source lets the administrator choose OpenAI, Anthropic or a compatible provider using their own key. Document text, page images and questions may be transmitted to that provider. Before hosted use, providers, contracts and transfer bases require approval; see the privacy notice and DPA drafts.
s.q6.a: The hosted server is at Contabo in Germany according to the operator decision. Email, backups and optional analysis services require separate checks; Germany is not a promise covering every data flow. Outstanding recipient details are identified in the legal drafts. Self-hosting operators determine their own processing.
s.r1.p: Each lease gets a statement that accounts for partial rental periods and vacancies. Costs are split by floor area, co-ownership shares (MEA), units, people, consumption or by hand. The statement takes the advance payments from the payments you posted. One run creates the drafts for the whole property; you check and finalize each statement, and then get its PDF and a suggestion for the new advance payment.
s.r2.p: Split into a base share and a consumption share, or you use the statement from your metering company.
s.r3.p: The Hausgeld the owners have paid is already included, and the asset report is modelled on § 28(4) WEG. The annual budget and the annual statement come out as PDFs for the owners' meeting.
s.r4.p: Import bank statements as CSV or CAMT.053 (XML or ZIP). Verwalino first shows what would be booked, spots transactions imported twice and suggests rent accounts; only what you confirm gets posted. You can split a payment across several accounts or reverse it.
s.r5.p: Collect monthly rent by direct debit: manage mandates and your creditor ID, and create the pain.008 file for your bank.
s.r6.p: Three reminder levels with a fee and late-payment interest (base rate plus 5 percentage points, § 288 BGB; you enter the base rate). The reminder run first shows who would get a reminder; the ones you select become drafts, from which you create the PDFs.
s.r7.p: Export accounting entries for your tax advisor in DATEV format (SKR03 or SKR04), plus CSV and an annual summary for each property.
s.r8.p: Upload an invoice, enter the amount and BetrKV cost type, and the cost item is done. Text recognition and e-invoices (XML) are handled by a background service that is currently switched off.

self.intro: Verwalino runs with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL on your server or laptop. The steps below apply to the current state on GitHub.
self.requirements.title: Prerequisites
self.requirements.body: Linux or macOS with Bash, OpenSSL, Docker Engine 24 or later (or Docker Desktop) and Docker Compose 2.24 or later. You do not need Python, Node or a separate proxy for the first installation.
self.commands.title: Three commands from the checkout
self.init.title: What init creates
self.init.body: `init` creates five different random 256-bit keys in the private file `.env.selfhost` (file mode 0600). Back up this file; an existing one is not overwritten. `start` builds the image from the checkout, waits for the database, runs the migrations and starts the app, locally at `http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
self.admin.title: The first administrator
self.admin.body: The third command creates the organization and its administrator and asks for the password twice without showing it. There is no default password, and existing users are left as they are. On an empty installation, `start` can instead print a `/setup` address and, separately, a one-time token valid for 24 hours. This browser route has not been released yet.
self.https.title: HTTPS with Caddy
self.https.body: For an installation reachable from the internet, choose HTTPS when you run `init`: `--https` `verwaltung.example.org`. The domain must point to the server, and ports 80 and 443 must be free. Caddy redirects HTTP to HTTPS and gets the certificates. Sign in through the HTTPS address and don’t expose the local HTTP port to the internet. Check that the certificate has been issued and the HTTPS address is reachable.
self.backup.title: Back up before changes
self.backup.body: Before an upgrade, run `bash scripts/self-host.sh backup` to archive the database and documents. `.env.selfhost` is not included; keep that file separately and encrypted. To restore, stop the app, load the archive with `restore` and start it again. Try this once on another machine so you know it works. There is no update command yet, and an older image does not roll back the database schema.
self.limits.title: What this installation does not yet support
self.limits.body: In the installation described here, email sending (SMTP), the optional document analysis and automatic invoice OCR are turned off; you enter invoices by hand. The signed public image is not published yet; `start` builds it from the checkout. Installation on a fresh server and use with a real domain and TLS are not yet cleared for production.
self.unreleased.title: Planned releases
self.unreleased.body: The source code is on GitHub under AGPL-3.0. Backup, restore and the doctor command are in the checkout. These parts are still missing or not yet released:
self.repository.body: `DEPLOY.md` in the public GitHub repository contains the full guide.

draft.checklist.title: Required before approval
draft.checklist.host: Q01/Q02: Confirm operator contact, hosting contracting entity, storage and access locations.
draft.checklist.processors: Q03/Q06/Q14: Establish email, AI and other recipients, contracts, international transfers and change notices.

draft.privacy.controller.title: 1. Controller and scope
draft.privacy.controller.body: {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, {operator.country}, represented by {operator.director}, is the controller for this website and hosted-service account, contract and operational data. Contact: {operator.privacyEmail}. This notice covers verwalino.de and the service at app.verwalino.de. Self-hosting operators are responsible for their own processing; this notice does not replace theirs. [OPEN Q11: Assess whether a DPO must be appointed and add their contact if applicable.]
draft.privacy.hosting.title: 2. Website, hosting and connection data
draft.privacy.hosting.body: The website serves static pages and local fonts. Your browser transmits connection data needed to deliver them, including its network address and requested resource. The website code contains no analytics, advertising or externally hosted font services. The operator decision places the server with Contabo in Germany. [OPEN Q02/Q05: Add the legal entity, address, data centre, other recipients and remote access locations, actual log fields and maximum log retention.] The purpose is delivery and protection of the service, with Article 6(1)(f) GDPR as the proposed basis. The interest is a secure, available service; document the balancing assessment and specific retention before approval.
draft.privacy.account.title: 3. Registration, account and contact
draft.privacy.account.body: Registration processes the organization name, your name, email address and password; a password hash and confirmation-token hash are stored. Roles, preferences, timestamps and security data are also processed. Contact details may instead be supplied by your organization administrator. Purposes are setup, login, account administration, necessary messages and support. Article 6(1)(b) GDPR applies where you personally are the contracting party or request pre-contractual steps; for a company customer’s employees and representatives, Article 6(1)(f) may support orderly provision and security of the service. Legally required handling of privacy requests is based on Article 6(1)(c) with Articles 12–22 GDPR. Required fields are necessary for setup and login; an account cannot be provided without them. No automated decision about you within Article 22 GDPR is made. [OPEN Q14: Add information delivery and evidenced contract formation to signup; the existing email confirmation does not record DPA acceptance.]
draft.privacy.properties.title: 4. Your property manager’s data
draft.privacy.properties.body: For management data entered or uploaded by a customer, fogu generally acts as processor under Article 28 GDPR. This includes tenancy, ownership, contact, bank, payment, accounting, consumption, document and communication data and related evidence. The customer determines purposes and legal bases and informs the people concerned. Where the manager itself acts for another controller, the contract and instruction chain must first be established. We forward requests about such data to the relevant customer and assist it. Account data and the operator’s own operational purposes are separate. Uploaded documents may contain particularly sensitive data; comprehensive technical filtering of such contents is not promised.
draft.privacy.storage.title: 5. Cookies and browser storage
draft.privacy.storage.body: The website itself sets no cookies. After you use the theme control it stores your selection as verwalino-theme in local storage and reads it on a later visit; it has no application expiry. You can clear it through browser settings. Language follows the URL. The app uses the hv_session login cookie, valid for two hours by default, with HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax; Secure must be enabled for HTTPS operation. Session storage holds confirmation and password-reset tokens during those flows and an economic-plan form draft with user/organization identity. Tokens are removed on success or final invalidity, and the draft when the form closes; session storage generally ends with the tab session. [OPEN Q13: Verify deployed settings and necessity for each purpose.] Section 25(2)(2) TDDDG is the proposed exception for storage strictly necessary for an explicitly requested service; otherwise prior consent is required. Calling a purpose functional does not establish the exception. Blanket consent to this privacy notice is not requested.
draft.privacy.email.title: 6. Email and recipients
draft.privacy.email.body: Account confirmation, password recovery and necessary service messages use the configured SMTP service. Customer-triggered document messages include recipient address, message and PDF and are sent on the customer’s behalf. The transport supports TLS; this is not end-to-end encryption. [OPEN Q03: Name the provider’s legal entity, locations, sub-processors and retention; check its DPA and the protection required for messages.] Other recipients include authorized staff, necessary advisers and authorities where legally required or for lawful claims. Customer data is not intended for publication. Bases for the operator’s own purposes are in section 3; customer messages are governed by its instructions and DPA.
draft.privacy.rights.title: 10. Your rights
draft.privacy.rights.body: Subject to statutory conditions you may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction and portability (Articles 15–20 GDPR). You may object to Article 6(1)(f) processing on grounds relating to your particular situation (Article 21); objection to direct marketing would be possible at any time. You may withdraw consent for the future without affecting earlier lawful processing. Contact: {operator.privacyEmail}. We normally respond within one month; any permitted extension of up to two further months is explained within the first month. We request only necessary identity-verification information. For customer data we assist the relevant controller; statutory exceptions, including records lawfully subject to retention, may prevent erasure. A technical deletion restriction alone is not a statutory exception.
draft.privacy.authority.title: 11. Complaints
draft.privacy.authority.body: Article 77 GDPR gives you the right to complain to a supervisory authority, particularly where you live, work or the alleged infringement occurred. The operator’s named authority is the Unabhängiges Datenschutzzentrum Saarland; contact and complaint channels: https://www.datenschutz.saarland.de. You do not have to contact us first.
draft.terms.scope.title: 1. Provider, eligible customers and service
draft.terms.scope.body: The provider of the free hosted Verwalino service is {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, represented by {operator.director}; contact: {operator.email}. The service supports rental, WEG and SEV management in separate organizations. It does not replace legal or tax advice or the manager’s review of results. The current project is not yet approved for public use with real management data. [OPEN Q09: Intended customers are exclusively businesses within section 14 BGB contracting in their own name; private landlords and homeowners’ associations are not automatically businesses. Establish eligibility and verification before approval.] AGPL-3.0 governs source code; these terms concern the hosted service, not an independently operated installation.
draft.terms.free.title: 3. Free service and limits
draft.terms.free.body: Hosted use is free of charge. A paid contract requires a separate express agreement. Current source limits per organization are 2 GiB of document storage, 25 MiB per upload, 20 properties and 200 units; the app displays usage and limits. External AI services commissioned by the customer may charge the customer. [OPEN Q06/Q09: Confirm approved scope and providers before contracting.] Free pricing does not remove security, privacy, return or statutory duties.
draft.terms.availability.title: 4. Operation and outages
draft.terms.availability.body: No specific availability percentage or continuous support coverage is promised. Planned significant outages are announced in advance where possible; necessary security measures may take effect immediately. Report problems to {operator.email}. [OPEN Q12: Establish actual support hours, deputies, backup and recovery arrangements.] This service description does not exclude statutory claims or agreed protection and return duties.
draft.terms.duties.title: 5. Customer duties
draft.terms.duties.body: The customer manages permissions, protects credentials and processes only data supported by a legal basis and any required consent. It checks calculations, assignments and documents before professional use or dispatch and reports detected errors. It avoids unnecessarily sensitive management data. Customer review does not remove the provider’s own duties. External analysis services may be used only after the approval procedure described in the DPA.
draft.terms.data.title: 6. Data, export and handover
draft.terms.data.body: The customer determines processing of management data under the DPA. Before service ends an organization administrator can download a .tar.gz archive containing authorized JSONL records, a checksum manifest, original files and payment/cost CSV files. Credentials, AI configuration and unauthorized evidence are excluded. The archive is available for 24 hours while authorization remains valid; it is not itself encrypted. Size, permission and integrity constraints mean re-import is not always possible. Export alone does not guarantee a tax-compliant migration. [OPEN Q07: Verify completeness, supplementary return and readability with the customer before termination and agree usable retention/audit access.] The customer protects received archives; this does not remove fogu’s own backup duties.
draft.terms.termination.title: 7. Termination, shutdown and account access
draft.terms.termination.body: [OPEN Q08 — proposal:] The customer may terminate at any time in text form. fogu may end the service on 90 days’ notice in text form, with export available until the agreed end. Termination for good cause remains available; protective measures are limited to what is necessary and secure return is arranged. Contract termination is distinct from technical erasure confirmation. Confirmation starts seven days of read-only access with export and cancellation, followed by operator execution. Seven days is the earliest execution time. After execution all accounts are disabled, with no continuing read-only login. A specific later execution deadline or replacement service is not yet promised. Before approval specify the termination route, funded handover, execution cadence and failed-erasure handling.
draft.terms.liability.title: 9. Liability
draft.terms.liability.body: [OPEN Q10 — proposal for counsel:] Statutory liability rules apply; this draft introduces no additional contractual limitation. In particular it does not exclude claims for intent, gross negligence, injury to life, body or health, or mandatory claims under Article 82 GDPR. Free pricing does not automatically establish a comprehensive exclusion. Whether gift or gratuitous-loan provisions, including sections 521 and 599 BGB, apply to this particular service requires legal classification. No zero-euro liability cap is agreed. Before approval assess contract type, insurance and any lawful differentiated clause.
draft.terms.law.title: 10. Law and priority
draft.terms.law.body: German law applies subject to mandatory applicable provisions. Following approval the German version is authoritative. Individually agreed terms take priority; the DPA prevails for conflicts concerning processing on behalf of customers. No exclusive jurisdiction clause is included. Invalid clauses are handled under statutory rules, without an automatic replacement preserving the closest economic effect.
draft.dpa.subject.title: 1. Parties, subject and duration
draft.dpa.subject.body: Processor: {operator.name}, {operator.street}, {operator.city}, {operator.country}, represented by {operator.director}, contact {operator.privacyEmail}. Customer: [complete legal name, legal form, address, representative, contact and organization reference]. The service is hosted Verwalino for rental, WEG and SEV management. Start: [date]; duration: until the main agreement ends, and for lawfully retained processing data until return/erasure is complete. Protection duties continue for that period. [OPEN Q07/Q14: Define continuing archive instructions and electronic conclusion with version evidence.] If the customer is itself a processor, record the controller and its authorization for this sub-processing; the instruction chain applies accordingly. Annex 1 (sections 2–4), annex 2 (9–13), annex 3 (14–16) and annex 4 (17) form part of this agreement.
draft.dpa.purpose.title: 2. Annex 1 — nature and purpose
draft.dpa.purpose.body: Processing supports the commissioned property-management service: collection by entry/import, organization, storage, retrieval, calculation, preparation of statements and correspondence, instructed dispatch, export, backup/recovery, restriction and erasure. Documents are read locally; external analysis is limited to separately authorized scope under annex 3. Operational/support access is limited to what the assignment requires. No own advertising, sale or training of own models using processing data. External providers must be contractually bound to this instruction; their actual terms still require review. fogu’s own account/contract and security purposes are separately described in the privacy notice.
draft.dpa.data.title: 3. Annex 1 — data categories
draft.dpa.data.body: Identity, address, communication and bank data; roles and user identifiers; leases, ownership, powers of attorney and service-provider contacts; rents, deposits, payments, arrears, bank movements, costs, invoices, statements, economic plans and asset reports; meter/consumption data; meeting, vote and resolution data; tasks, messages, signatures, uploaded and generated originals; editing, access, provenance and dispatch evidence. Approved AI use additionally covers transmitted questions, text/image extracts, results and usage data. Article 9/10 data is not an intended separate purpose but may occur in free text or attachments. [OPEN Q09/Q11: Agree necessary sensitive categories, permitted scope and additional safeguards with the customer; exclude unnecessary data.]
draft.dpa.subjects.title: 4. Annex 1 — data subjects
draft.dpa.subjects.body: Tenants and co-tenants, owners and former owners, representatives and authorized agents, service providers and their contacts, customer employees/users, and other people mentioned in lawfully submitted records. [Before conclusion the customer must confirm actual groups, add particularly vulnerable groups where relevant, and remove unused groups.]
draft.dpa.duties.title: 5. Instructions, confidentiality and legality
draft.dpa.duties.body: fogu processes data only on documented customer instructions, including transfers, unless EU or Member State law requires other processing. It then informs the customer before processing unless prohibited by law on important public-interest grounds. Customer instruction contacts/deputies: [complete]; fogu contacts/deputies: [complete, OPEN Q12]; initial documented channel {operator.privacyEmail}, with an agreed protected channel for sensitive contents. Urgent oral instructions are documented promptly. If fogu considers an instruction unlawful, it informs the customer immediately and resolves the affected processing before continuing. Authorized persons are bound to confidentiality or a statutory duty of secrecy; access is limited to necessity. fogu maintains its processing record and cooperates with the competent authority.
draft.dpa.tom.title: 9. Annex 2 — safeguards and evidence status
draft.dpa.tom.body: fogu undertakes to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures under Article 32 GDPR considering risk, state of the art and cost. The following describes source capabilities and documented operating procedures; it does not prove actual deployment. [OPEN Q12: Before conclusion record implementation, accountable role, check date and private evidence for every measure.] Equivalent improvements are permitted without reducing the agreed protection. Material changes are documented and coordinated with the customer where they affect agreed protection. No certification is claimed.
draft.dpa.processors.title: 14. Annex 3 — recipients and sub-processor register
draft.dpa.processors.body: Complete each row before conclusion: legal entity/address; service and data categories; storage, processing and support countries; further sub-processors; DPA/safeguard evidence; authorization and date; transfer basis; deletion period. Hosting: Contabo, Germany per operator decision — exact entity, address and contract/access locations [OPEN Q02]. SMTP: [provider, places and periods OPEN Q03]. External backups: [provider/location or verified absence of external recipient, OPEN Q04]. Error tracking: self-hosted GlitchTip is documented, actual host/recipient [OPEN Q05]. Optional AI: OpenAI, Anthropic or a compatible endpoint are technically available, but are not an approved provider list [OPEN Q06]. Assess maintenance suppliers with possible data access too. Local OCR is not itself a sub-processor. Open entries do not constitute authorization; a completed list is required for each use.
draft.dpa.controller.title: 8. Customer duties and audit rights
draft.dpa.controller.body: The customer is responsible for purposes, lawful bases, notices, lawful instructions and required upstream sub-processing authorization. fogu makes available all information demonstrating Article 28 compliance and allows and contributes to audits, including inspections, by the customer or its appointed auditor. Meaningful evidence may be reviewed first, without excluding necessary on-site inspection. Scope and timing are reasonably coordinated where the reason and urgency permit; incidents, justified suspicion or authority requirements are not subject to blanket annual or advance-notice limits. Other customers’ data and trade secrets are protected without frustrating the audit. This draft imposes no fee that prevents statutory audit or assistance.
draft.dpa.deletion.title: 17. Annex 4 — return, service exit and erasure
draft.dpa.deletion.body: After the service ends, at the customer’s choice fogu returns or erases processing data and deletes existing copies unless a specific applicable statutory storage duty prevents this. Continued archiving for customer obligations requires documented continuing instructions; the customer’s retention duty is not automatically fogu’s own duty. Before account closure a permission-checked .tar.gz archive is available with JSONL, checksum manifest, originals and payment/cost CSV; download lasts at most 24 hours and cleanup is a separate job. Unauthorized evidence and credentials are excluded and importability is limited. [OPEN Q07: Supplement missing data lawfully due for return and verify handover/readability.] Erasure confirmation starts seven days of read-only access with export/cancellation; subsequent execution is by the operator, not automatic on day seven. Afterwards there is no customer login; unbound data is erased/minimized while protected originals, evidence and dependencies remain restricted. Current source has no automatic final purge of these remnants. [OPEN Q04/Q07/Q08: Before conclusion agree and implement execution time, residual categories/bases/end dates, an accessible retrieval route, separate archiving, final erasure and maximum age for every backup copy.] Server rotation of 14 daily/8 weekly generations plus ten labelled backups is insufficient on its own. Restores must reconcile later erasures. fogu records execution, remaining copies, reasons/periods and subsequent complete erasure. Indefinite retention is not agreed.
draft.authoritative: Following approval, the German version is authoritative. This draft is not an executed contract or legal advice. [OPEN Qxx] marks an outstanding operator decision.
draft.download: Download the DPA and annexes as Markdown
imprint.contact.review: [OPEN Q01: Before approval, add another means of rapid, direct communication and a business identification number if applicable. The company details come from the operator decision and require confirmation that they remain current.]
draft.privacy.ai.title: 7. Optional document analysis and international transfers
draft.privacy.ai.body: OCR can run locally. Optional document analysis and property questions can send document text, page images, questions and context to the provider chosen by the organization administrator. The source supports OpenAI, Anthropic and compatible endpoints using a customer key; such a key guarantees neither a particular location nor zero retention. [OPEN Q06: Before approval establish exact providers, contractual roles, data scope, countries including support, retention and contractual exclusion of training.] Third-country processing must first have a verified basis under Articles 44 onwards GDPR; add the actual basis and how to obtain safeguards here before activation. A server in Germany does not exclude these transfers.
draft.privacy.security.title: 8. Security, error reporting and support
draft.privacy.security.body: Login attempts are counted using pseudonymous network/email keys to prevent abuse. Error logs support troubleshooting. Optional error tracking is off without a configured destination; self-hosted GlitchTip is documented for hosting. Filters remove many sensitive contents, but identifiers and remaining information are not thereby anonymous. Diagnostic bundles are shared manually. The operator’s own security and support purposes require the Article 6(1)(f) balancing assessment. [OPEN Q05/Q12: Confirm actual log fields, recipients, access and deletion periods; never attach customer documents to public error reports.]
draft.privacy.retention.title: 9. Retention and service exit
draft.privacy.retention.body: Accounts remain during use. Signup links last 24 hours; confirmed requests are removed, while expired requests become eligible for usage-dependent cleanup seven days after expiry. Password-reset links last one hour. These are not guaranteed deletion periods for all related data. Organization archives can be downloaded for 24 hours while authorization remains valid; file cleanup must run separately. Confirmed organization erasure starts seven days of read-only access with export and cancellation; the operator executes erasure afterwards. Accounts are disabled and certain records/evidence remain restricted. There is no automatic final purge of that evidence. Backups rotate by generation rather than a verified maximum age for every copy. [OPEN Q04/Q05/Q07/Q08: Before approval establish complete periods, bases for remaining data, backup expiry and the request route after account closure.] Details are in the terms and DPA. This does not authorize indefinite stockpiling.
draft.privacy.sources.title: Legal sources and review date
draft.privacy.sources.body: Checked on 12 November 2026: GDPR, particularly Articles 5, 6, 12–22, 28, 32 and 44 onwards: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj; section 25 TDDDG: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ttdsg/__25.html; section 38 BDSG: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bdsg_2018/__38.html. Resolve the open entries before using this as complete information under Articles 13/14 GDPR.
draft.terms.contract.title: 2. Contract formation and DPA
draft.terms.contract.body: [OPEN Q14 — proposal:] Before activation an authorized customer accepts the specific terms version and electronically concludes the completed DPA with its annexes; both are provided in a permanently savable form. The contract starts with fogu’s confirmed acceptance. The current signup email confirmation alone does not replace this step. Personal management data must not be entered before conclusion. A privacy notice informs about processing; it is not blanket consent. Material contractual changes require a valid agreement; these terms do not treat silence alone as acceptance.
draft.terms.retention.title: 8. Retention and erasure
draft.terms.retention.body: Return or erasure follows the customer’s choice and Article 28(3)(g) GDPR; legally necessary residual retention must have a specific basis. Customer tax and commercial duties may require ten, eight or six years, or longer where applicable, depending on the record (section 147 AO, section 257 HGB). Using Verwalino alone does not fulfil them. The source retains protected records, evidence and dependencies and partly uses provisional eight-year periods; it has no automatic final purge. A maximum age for all backup copies has not been verified. [OPEN Q04/Q07: Before approval establish and implement the legal basis, continuing archive instruction, operator retrieval, periods, deletion of copies and evidence.] These limitations do not authorize indefinite retention or replace complete return.
draft.terms.sources.title: Legal sources and review date
draft.terms.sources.body: Checked on 12 November 2026: sections 305 onwards, particularly 307, 309, 310, and sections 516 onwards and 598 onwards BGB: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/; Articles 28, 82 GDPR: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj; section 147 AO: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__147.html; section 257 HGB: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__257.html. Contract classification and fairness of clauses remain unresolved.
draft.dpa.assistance.title: 6. Rights and assistance
draft.dpa.assistance.body: Taking account of the nature of processing, fogu provides appropriate measures to assist with requests under Articles 12–22 GDPR. Customer-data requests received by fogu are forwarded promptly; fogu answers only on customer instructions unless it has its own legal duty. It provides available data and information in time for the customer’s deadlines and assists rectification, restriction, transfer and lawful erasure. Taking account of available information, it also assists Articles 32–36 duties, including risk assessment, DPIAs and prior consultation. A product export is not a substitute for a complete data-subject access response. [OPEN Q12: Assign responsible staff and achievable response times before conclusion.]
draft.dpa.breach.title: 7. Personal-data breaches
draft.dpa.breach.body: fogu notifies the customer without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach affecting its processing data, without treating 72 hours as a waiting period. The initial notice includes available details of nature, affected data/subject categories and approximate numbers, contact, likely consequences and measures taken/proposed; missing information follows without undue further delay. fogu preserves necessary evidence, limits harm and assists notification/communication under Articles 33/34 GDPR. Decisions remain with the customer as controller; fogu’s own statutory duties remain unaffected. [OPEN Q12: Enter reachable incident contacts and deputies for both parties.]
draft.dpa.tom_access.title: 10. Annex 2 — confidentiality and separation
draft.dpa.tom_access.body: Present in source: organization RLS and composite foreign keys; additional source/data-domain permissions; role checks and separate runtime/maintenance privileges; Argon2 password hashes; signed HttpOnly sessions revoked on relevant account changes; login limiting; local document storage and private export files. HTTPS with Caddy and SMTP TLS are documented operating paths. [OPEN Q02/Q03/Q12: Evidence TLS/Secure-cookie configuration, actual administrator rights, MFA for privileged operational access, access reviews, device security and host physical controls.] RLS does not prevent every privileged operator access. Full database/original encryption at rest or end-to-end encryption is not asserted as deployed.
draft.dpa.tom_integrity.title: 11. Annex 2 — integrity, traceability and minimization
draft.dpa.tom_integrity.body: Present: database guards against unlawful changes to confirmed financial data, original-file hash checks, editing/provenance evidence, permission-checked exports and bounded document processing. Error reports are scrubbed and secret fields are excluded from exports. Immutable evidence can remain personal data. [OPEN Q05/Q12: Evidence log access, detection/response, change approval, patch cadence and regular effectiveness checks.] A hash and technical immutability guard alone are not a GoBD attestation.
draft.dpa.tom_availability.title: 12. Annex 2 — availability and recovery
draft.dpa.tom_availability.body: Documented backups pair database and documents, with private configuration additionally included in the server format. They initially reside on the same server; this alone does not cover server loss. Rotation keeps 14 daily/8 weekly unlabelled generations and ten newest labelled backups; it is not a fixed maximum age for every copy. [OPEN Q04/Q12: Add the actual schedule, separate encrypted location, key management, maximum age including labelled copies, recovery objectives and successful restore tests.] Deletions and access revocations after a backup must be reconciled before restored service is reopened; fully automatic reconciliation is not claimed.
draft.dpa.tom_organization.title: 13. Annex 2 — organization and rights
draft.dpa.tom_organization.body: Existing tools support access, permission-checked export, restriction and organization erasure with retention reconciliation. [OPEN Q07/Q12: Establish and evidence confidentiality commitments, training, access reviews, instruction/incident registers, supplier review, incident deputies and deadline tracking.] Retention expiry and deletion of final copies require a separate procedure; protected evidence currently has no automatic final purge. Evaluate effectiveness regularly and after material changes; provide the customer with necessary private evidence.
draft.dpa.changes.title: 15. Annex 3 — authorization and changes
draft.dpa.changes.body: [OPEN Q14 — proposal:] The customer gives general written authorization only for the register completed at conclusion. fogu provides at least 30 days’ advance notice in text form of intended additions/replacements, with tasks, data, countries and safeguards; the customer may object on privacy grounds within 21 days. Processing by the new provider does not start before the notice period ends or while a justified objection remains unresolved. The parties seek an equivalent alternative; otherwise the affected service may end without penalty, with secure return. Urgent exceptions require specific prior authorization. fogu imposes the same privacy duties on sub-processors and remains responsible to the customer for their performance (Article 28(4) GDPR). Merely editing a webpage does not replace notification.
draft.dpa.transfers.title: 16. Annex 3 — locations and international processing
draft.dpa.transfers.body: Hosting in Germany is not a promise that every data flow stays there. [OPEN Q06: Establish the role and contract chain for each AI endpoint and other recipient; a customer key or customer-entered URL does not remove fogu’s own duties.] Processing or access outside the EU/EEA requires documented instructions/authorization and compliance with Articles 44 onwards GDPR. Before processing, record and make available the specific adequacy decision with verified scope or appropriate safeguards, including required transfer assessment and supplementary measures. Blanket customer consent does not replace this assessment. A flow is not approved while its recipient or basis remains unresolved.
draft.dpa.completion.title: 18. Conclusion and priority
draft.dpa.completion.body: Following approval the German version is authoritative; this agreement prevails over conflicting main-agreement provisions on processing. Statutory data-subject rights, supervisory powers and Article 82 GDPR remain unaffected. Changes and instructions are documented; Article 28(9) permits electronic form. Complete all open entries and annexes before conclusion; actual customer data, signatures and internal security evidence must not enter the public repository. Customer: [name/authority, date, signature or electronic acceptance evidence]. fogu: [representative, date, signature or electronic acceptance evidence]. Contract/annex version: [complete]. Operator and counsel approval: [outstanding].
